CVE-2025-13327.title: A flaw was found in uv. This vulnerability allows an attacker to  ...
CVE-2025-13327.description: A flaw was found in uv. This vulnerability allows an attacker to execute malicious code during package resolution or installation via specially crafted ZIP (Zipped Information Package) archives that exploit parsing differentials, requiring user interaction to install an attacker-controlled package.

CVE-2025-54368.title: uv is a Python package and project manager written in Rust. In ve ...
CVE-2025-54368.description: uv is a Python package and project manager written in Rust. In versions 0.8.5 and earlier, remote ZIP archives were handled in a streamwise fashion, and file entries were not reconciled against the archive's central directory. An attacker could contrive a ZIP archive that would extract with legitimate contents on some package installers, and malicious contents on others due to multiple local file entries. An attacker could  also contrive a "stacked" ZIP input with multiple internal ZIPs, which would be handled differently by different package installers. The attacker could choose which installer to target in both scenarios. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.6. To work around this issue, users may choose to set UV_INSECURE_NO_ZIP_VALIDATION=1 to revert to the previous behavior.

CVE-2025-71437.title: Astral uv before 0.8.22 contains a path traversal vulnerability i ...
CVE-2025-71437.description: Astral uv before 0.8.22 contains a path traversal vulnerability in source distribution (sdist) tar extraction that allows a specially crafted sequence of symlinks to redirect file writes outside the intended extraction prefix. Attackers can publish a malicious sdist that, when installed by a victim, writes arbitrary files to filesystem locations outside the installation prefix.

CVE-2026-114109.title: uv before 0.11.15 contains a path traversal vulnerability that al ...
CVE-2026-114109.description: uv before 0.11.15 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows malicious wheels to write files outside the scripts directory via crafted console_scripts or gui_scripts entry point names. Attackers who induce users to install a malicious wheel can place executables in PATH directories, shadowing or overwriting existing binaries for code execution.

CVE-2026-114110.title: Astral uv before 0.11.6 contains a path traversal vulnerability t ...
CVE-2026-114110.description: Astral uv before 0.11.6 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows attackers to delete arbitrary files by supplying wheels with relative traversal paths in RECORD entries. Attackers can craft a malicious wheel whose RECORD references files outside the installation prefix, causing uv to delete those files when the user uninstalls the package.

CVE-2026-119327.title: Removal of emSign root certificate
CVE-2026-119327.description: ### Summary **This is a widespread incident that affects the entire open source ecosystem. If you use any software that depends on vendored CA bundles via packages like `certifi` or `webpki-root-certs`, you MUST upgrade it. uv is not the only impacted package. You MUST evaluate your other packages.** Intermediate certificates issued by the `emSign ECC Root CA - G3` root CA are considered compromised. A compromised CA can be used to impersonate websites, circumventing the integrity and authenticity controls of HTTPS. uv 0.13.4 removes this root CA from its vendored CA bundle (following webpki-root-certs). Users should upgrade to 0.13.4 immediately, or otherwise confirm that their usage either uses the system CA certificates (`--system-certs`) or custom certificates (`SSL_CERT_FILE` or `SSL_CERT_DIR`) and that neither of those contain the compromised intermediates or their roots. ### Details The `emSign ECC Root CA - G3` root CA issued intermediate CA certificates whose keys are compromised. Connections that chain through those intermediates should be considered insecure. See https://github.com/rustls/webpki-roots/releases/tag/v%2F1.0.10 and https://github.com/certifi/python-certifi/security/advisories/GHSA-6q48-6c7w-9gw2 for additional context. Users are affected if they use uv's bundled CA certificates, which are used by default. Users who use system certificates instead should consult their system's certificate store to ensure that the root and/or its compromised intermediates are already distrusted by their operating system. Users who use a custom CA file or directory should confirm that their custom bundle(s) do not contain the compromised intermediates and/or their roots. ### Proof of concept See: - https://github.com/certifi/python-certifi/security/advisories/GHSA-6q48-6c7w-9gw2 - https://emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/ - https://groups.google.com/a/mozilla.org/g/dev-security-policy/c/0R3XLJL6FuE/m/0XofdebrAAAJ ### Impact A compromised key for a certificate authority can be used to issue certificates to enable MITM attacks.

GHSA-4gg8-gxpx-9rph.title: uv is vulnerable to arbitrary file write through entry point names
GHSA-4gg8-gxpx-9rph.description:
### Impact

In versions of uv prior to 0.11.15, when installing a distribution containing an entry point specification (under `console_scripts` or `gui_scripts`), uv would place the generated entry point according to the given name even if doing so resulted in a path outside of the environment's scripts directory.

A malicious wheel could use this to place an executable outside of the intended environment, including in a directory already present on the user's `PATH`. This could shadow or overwrite an existing executable and potentially result in unexpected code execution under the wheel's control, even if the wheel's installation environment was not explicitly added to `PATH` by the user.

In order to exploit this vulnerability, the attacker must induce their target into installing a malicious wheel.

### Patches

uv 0.11.15 and newer address this vulnerability. Users are encouraged to upgrade to 0.11.15.

### Workarounds

There is no workaround other than upgrading to uv 0.11.15.
